newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on higher overnight rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on higher overnight rates.

text.p: * Peso average at 26.243 from 26.264 to the dollar
The Philippine peso closed stronger on Wednesday at 26.249 from 26.255 as banks continued to unload their dollars in view of the high interest rates in the money market, traders said.
The average interbank call loan rate shot up to 14 percent on Wednesday from 12.28125.
"There was artificial tightness in the overnight market," said a dealer.
He added that banks were doing some speculative play on interest rates after the Central Bank raised its overnight lending rate to 15 from 13 percent on Tuesday.
To cap the peso's strength, the Central Bank stepped aggressively in mid-morning after the peso reached a day-high of 26.235 to the dollar, traders said.
One dealer estimated the Central Bank purchased about $55 million, initially at 26.241 and later up to 26.249.
Turnover was higher marginally at $183.30 million from $182.60 million.
Looking ahead, a trader said the peso is expected to slightly depreciate in the next few days.
"The Central Bank's agenda is over. It punished banks who bought dollars with no legitimate demand when it raised its interest rate," said the dealer.
Moreover, he said the Central Bank is now aggressively buying dollars again which should limit the strenght of the peso.
And since Central Bank bought about $90 million the past days, this should add about 2.3 billion pesos to liquidity and ease interest rates, he said.
